Washer at 1,383 rpm (posterior P=1.0), scale uncalibrated. Reporting findings before optimising — resonance is the leading hypothesis, with several faults non-evaluable above the 15 Hz video Nyquist.

title: Resonance: 1x critical at 551 rpm within swept range
summary: Fault posterior resonance P=0.65 (prior 0.12, +11.4 dB). Campbell critical: 1x crosses 9.18 Hz mode at 550.6 rpm (9.177 Hz x 60), inside the swept range, Q=21.9 quoted. Current speed 1,382.9 rpm (23.05 Hz) is 2.51x that critical, so this is a ramp-through resonance, not steady-state at present speed. Caution: the 9.18 Hz mode damping is zeta=0.00 +/-0.026 from half-power - damping/Q is poorly constrained, so amplitude at crossing is uncertain. Amplitudes are relative only (scale_calibrated=false); no ISO zone reported.

title: Structural modes 2.3-6.1 Hz identified; top panel dominant relatively
summary: FDD modes: 2.285 Hz zeta=5.35% sv_ratio=17.3, 3.340 Hz zeta=3.65% sv_ratio=29.3, 4.453 Hz zeta=2.84% sv_ratio=105.1, 6.094 Hz zeta=2.29% sv_ratio=51.8, channels washer front/top panels. Phases in FDD shapes are near 0 deg on 2nd channel reference; 4.453 Hz front phase -50.0 deg. Uncalibrated velocities s1=150.4 and s2=329.3 mm/s RMS are physically implausible / relative only - use only ratio s2/s1=2.19x, frequencies, phases and ratios, not absolute mm/s or ISO 20816 zones.

title: Possible looseness - weak, corroboration needed
summary: Looseness P=0.25 (prior 0.08): 9 shaft harmonics 1-10x above 10 dB (+9.6 dB) supports many-harmonics pattern, but half-order lines 4.5 dB give -3.8 dB counter-evidence. Not conclusive. No rubbing/impacts heard in audio (rubbing_or_impacts=false). Inspect mounts/feet/panel fixings only as part of resonance work order, do not diagnose looseness alone on this evidence.

title: Imbalance/misalignment/cavitation not evaluable at 23 Hz vs 15 Hz Nyquist
summary: Speed posterior MAP 1,382.9 rpm, CI68 1,382.9-1,385.0 rpm, p_map=1.0, 17/18 peaks explained, no display_rpm check available. However 1x=23.05 Hz exceeds video Nyquist 15.0 Hz (30 fps, near_nyquist_warning=true) and orders_vel 1x/2x/3x are all 0.0, so imbalance P=0.15, misalignment P=0.10, bearing/cavitation/flow all evaluable=false at prior values - no conclusion possible. Cavitation index 0.349, HF energy 7.7%, kurtosis 0.24 and audio cavitation_like=false do not support cavitation for this washer. Request better capture: accelerometer/tachometer or >=120 fps video (Nyquist > 2-3x 23 Hz) with a calibrated scale reference to evaluate 1x/2x amplitude and phase and ISO severity.

text: Reported. The washer is variable-speed with a critical at 551 rpm — running the digital-twin optimiser to find a speed clear of it.

Optimiser is feasible: 1,107 rpm vs 1,383 rpm current, −48.7% modelled energy and vibration, duty at the 80% floor, P(resonance)=0% at the proposed speed. Sending that setpoint for approval, noting the 551 rpm critical is still crossed on ramp.

rationale: Propose 1107.2 rpm (from 1382.9 rpm), feasible band 1107.2-1382.9 rpm. Duty: 80% of current, meets 80% minimum. Twin predicts kW 0.100 -> 0.051 (-48.7%) and vibration -48.7% (relative only; measured scale is uncalibrated, so do not use the twin's 0.00 mm/s as an ISO zone). Resonance margin: 1107 rpm is 2.01x the 550.6 rpm 1x critical (9.18 Hz mode), well beyond the 10% margin, and optimiser P(resonance)=0% at proposed speed; ramp-up/down will still cross 551 rpm, so pair with skip/fast-ramp below. NPSH: not applicable to this washer (not a centrifugal pump); audio shows no cavitation-like crackle. Human approval required before changing speed.

result.markdown:
# WO-261104-BB32D · Washer W-1

**Priority:** P2 (within 7 days)  
**Failure mode:** VIB – Vibration (ISO 14224)  
**Suspected cause:** Forcing frequency coincident with a structural natural frequency (posterior 0.65)  
**Raised by:** muse-wonder-1.0 · 2026-11-04 10:09

Resonance is the leading fault (P=0.65): 1x crosses the 9.18 Hz structural mode at 550.6 rpm during spin ramp, with FDD cabinet modes at 2.29, 3.34, 4.45 and 6.09 Hz. Inspect drum suspension, mounts/feet, counterweights and front/top panel fixings for looseness or damage (secondary looseness P=0.25), and confirm the drive does not dwell at 496-606 rpm. Re-capture with an accelerometer/tachometer or >=120 fps calibrated video, as the present 30 fps / 15 Hz Nyquist capture cannot evaluate 1x at 23.05 Hz.

## Evidence
- critical speed inside the swept range (Q) = 21.9 (+11.4 dB)
- Amplitudes uncalibrated: severity from frequencies and ratios
- Running speed 1383 rpm (audio (blade pass) · kinematic posterior (×0.299))

## Safety
- Lock out / tag out (LOTO) the drive and isolate process energy
- Guards back on before restart; no loose clothing near rotating parts

## Tasks
1. Program VFD skip frequencies over the resonance bands (Argonaut can do this).
2. If the duty needs that speed: detune the structure. To move fn above the forcing by 15 %, stiffness must rise by the factor computed below (mass unchanged). Here: fn = 9.18 Hz, 1x = 23.05 Hz -> stiffness x8.34 (fn ∝ √k).
3. Re-run a coast-down; confirm the Campbell crossing has moved out of the operating range.

## Parts
- Bracing / stiffener per detuning calculation

**Estimated time:** 1.0 h

## Verification
Re-measure with Argonaut after the work; acceptance: fault posterior < 0.2 and ISO zone A/B (or unchanged frequencies/ratios if uncalibrated).

text:
## Assessment — Washer W-1

**Identification**
- Running speed: **1,382.9 rpm (23.05 Hz)**, Bayesian MAP probability **1.00**, 68% CI **1,382.9–1,385.0 rpm**, 17/18 peaks explained. No display-rpm check was available.
- Variable-speed capture shows a **1× critical at 550.6 rpm**, where 1× crosses the **9.18 Hz** structural mode. FDD cabinet modes were also identified at **2.29, 3.34, 4.45 and 6.09 Hz**.
- Top-to-front panel relative amplitude ratio is approximately **2.19:1**.

**Important measurement limitation**
- `scale_calibrated=false`: amplitudes are **relative only**, so no ISO 20816 zone or absolute mm/s severity is reported.
- Capture Nyquist is **15.0 Hz**, below the present 1× frequency of **23.05 Hz**. Reported 1×/2×/3× order amplitudes are all 0.0. Consequently, imbalance, misalignment, bearing defect and cavitation are **not evaluable** in this capture.
- Requested better capture: calibrated accelerometer/tachometer measurement, or video at **≥120 fps**, covering spin ramp and steady operation.

## Diagnosis

1. **Resonance — leading fault, P=0.65**  
   The 1× critical is inside the swept speed range, with quoted Q=21.9 and evidence of **+11.4 dB**. At the present 1,382.9 rpm the machine is above the critical; the concern is principally amplification while accelerating/decelerating through approximately **551 rpm**. Damping for the 9.18 Hz mode is poorly constrained at ζ=0.00 ±0.026, so crossing amplitude remains uncertain.

2. **Looseness — possible but weak, P=0.25**  
   Nine shaft harmonics support the pattern, but half-order evidence is negative. This warrants physical inspection of suspension, mounts, counterweights and panel fixings, not a standalone looseness conclusion.

3. **Imbalance — not actionable**  
   Posterior remains at its prior value, **P=0.15**, and is non-evaluable. A balancing action was therefore **not proposed**. Cavitation is likewise unsupported: cavitation index **0.349**, HF energy fraction **0.077**, and audio was not cavitation-like.

## Optimisation

The constrained digital-twin optimisation is feasible at the required minimum duty:

- **Current:** 1,382.9 rpm, modelled **0.100 kW**
- **Proposed:** **1,107.2 rpm**, modelled **0.051 kW**
- Duty: **80% of current**, meeting the 80% minimum
- Expected modelled change: **−48.7% energy and −48.7% vibration**
- Feasible band: **1,107.2–1,382.9 rpm**
- Modelled resonance probability at proposed speed: **0%**
- The proposal remains well above the 550.6 rpm critical, but the machine will still cross that critical during ramp-up and coast-down.

**Setpoint proposal p67155 has been sent for human approval.** It must not be applied automatically.

An automated **skip-band action was not queued** because the optimiser identified no exclusion band within the proposed operating band. Avoiding dwell around 496–606 rpm is instead included in the work order for drive/ramp configuration review.

## Actions queued

- **Work order WO-261104-BB32D**, priority P2, due within 7 days: inspect suspension, mounts/feet, counterweights and panel fixings; check ramp behaviour around the 551 rpm crossing; then perform a calibrated re-measurement/coast-down.
- **Impact calculated by the tool:** 0.0487 kW saved while running, **292.0 kWh/year, $35.04/year and 0.131 t CO₂/year**, using its assumptions of 6,000 h/year, $0.12/kWh and 0.45 kg CO₂/kWh. These annual figures should be replaced with site operating hours, tariff and emission factor if different.
- **Follow-up re-measurement:** due **2026-12-04**, using a calibrated high-rate capture to verify the setpoint, evaluate 1×/2× properly, and confirm that resonance posterior falls below the work-order acceptance level of 0.2.
